title: Nine WebView test modules can hang indefinitely because Node subprocesses have no timeout
observed_behavior: Ten subprocess.run calls across nine test modules launch Node without a timeout. The embedded JavaScript has substantive assertions and the Python callers check exit status, but a non-terminating imported script, leaked timer, deadlocked promise, or generator regression leaves the test process waiting without a local deadline.
expected_invariant: Every external process launched by validation tests must have a bounded deadline and actionable timeout evidence so one hung JavaScript harness cannot stall a local gate or CI job indefinitely.
root_cause: These direct Node harnesses were implemented independently instead of using one bounded subprocess helper; nine modules omitted subprocess.run(timeout=...) even though a neighboring pipeline-log harness and the shared browser helper already demonstrate bounded execution.
failure_scenario: A WebView asset or ledger generator retains an event-loop handle, awaits a promise that never settles, or otherwise stops producing a terminal Node exit. The focused test, canonical gate, or audit worker hangs until an unrelated outer job timeout kills the entire run, obscuring the responsible module and delaying every downstream validation result.
evidence: AST inspection of every assigned WebView test found exactly ten Node subprocess.run calls without a timeout in the listed nine files
tests/webview/test_webview_pipeline_log_window_static.py lines 224-231 contains a comparable Node subprocess with timeout=30, showing the repository already uses a bounded pattern
the nine-module focused pack completed in the reviewed run, so this is a deterministic missing bound rather than a claim that the current JavaScript always hangs
all listed callers either assert the return code or use check=True; assertion strength does not bound process lifetime
affected_flows: local WebView static and Node smoke validation
CI or release validation that collects these modules
audit reproduction of command replay, lifecycle, diagnostics, rerun, log-window, and touchpoint contracts
existing_safeguards: the Node programs use explicit throws/assertions for semantic failures
Python callers validate nonzero exit status
some CI runners may impose a coarse job-level timeout
safeguard_gap: A coarse job timeout cannot identify or isolate the hung module and can discard unrelated results; none of the ten listed calls owns a process-level deadline or emits a module-specific timeout failure.
tests_present: the reviewed modules cover successful and negative JavaScript contract behavior
tests/webview/test_webview_pipeline_log_window_static.py already exercises one separately bounded Node invocation
tests_missing: a shared test proving a deliberately non-terminating Node child is killed within the configured deadline
a static guard rejecting direct subprocess.run Node invocations without timeout
recommended_remediation: Route these direct Node invocations through a shared bounded helper or add explicit conservative timeout values to every call, convert TimeoutExpired into a concise module-specific assertion, and ensure any spawned descendants are terminated where applicable.
remediation_risk: Low to medium: deadlines must leave headroom for slow Windows CI and diagnostics must preserve bounded stdout/stderr, while descendant cleanup needs platform-aware handling.
validation_rung: Rung 1 targeted WebView unit/static execution plus a synthetic hanging-Node timeout test; representative real-media validation is not required.
prior_audit_relationship: The interrupted W11 error artifact identified and deduplicated these calls but did not publish a finding fragment. This resumed review independently re-ran the AST inventory, read each call site at its current hash, and found no existing current finding with these test-path locations.

title: An inner browser-smoke timeout can kill Node while leaving its Chrome or Edge child alive
observed_behavior: run_node_browser_smoke bounds the Node runner with subprocess.run(timeout=...), but Python's timeout handling terminates that direct Node process. The generated runner starts Chrome or Edge as a Node child and relies on the runner's JavaScript finally block calling terminateBrowser. If Python kills Node at the inner deadline, that finally block cannot run and the browser process tree is not explicitly reclaimed by the helper.
expected_invariant: A browser smoke helper must own and terminate the complete process tree on success, assertion failure, runner crash, and every timeout path so disposable profiles, debugging ports, and browser processes cannot survive the test.
root_cause: Browser ownership is split across Python and generated JavaScript: Python owns the timeout but only sees Node, while JavaScript owns the browser handle and cleanup. No job object, process-group contract, parent-side browser PID handoff, or post-timeout tree termination bridges the two owners.
failure_scenario: A CDP wait or page script hangs beyond timeout_seconds. Python kills Node and promptly reports an assertion, so a longer outer PowerShell timeout never activates its process-tree cleanup. Chrome or Edge remains alive with the disposable user-data directory or debugging port open, causing profile cleanup failures, port conflicts, resource exhaustion, or later browser-smoke flakiness.
evidence: run_node_browser_smoke lines 219-236 uses subprocess.run(timeout=timeout_seconds) and translates TimeoutExpired into an assertion without a descendant cleanup step
browser_cdp_runner_prelude lines 386-405 launches the browser from Node and implements cleanup only through the Node-resident terminateBrowser function
every reviewed browser smoke uses disposable roots and JavaScript finally cleanup during ordinary completion, but those safeguards depend on Node remaining alive
the canonical PowerShell wrapper's process-tree cleanup is tied to its own longer outer timeout and does not run merely because the inner helper returned a timeout assertion
affected_flows: local and CI WebView smoke reliability
existing_safeguards: browser runners call terminateBrowser in JavaScript finally blocks
terminateBrowser escalates from normal kill to SIGKILL with bounded waits
Python bounds Node execution and browser tests use disposable temporary roots
the outer browser-smoke wrapper can kill a process tree on its own timeout
safeguard_gap: The inner timeout returns before the outer timeout and destroys the only process holding the browser handle, bypassing both the JavaScript finally cleanup and the outer tree-timeout path.
tests_present: tests/python/desktop/test_browser_smoke_support.py covers helper formatting and ordinary support behavior
browser-backed WebView modules exercise normal launch and JavaScript-finally cleanup
tests_missing: a forced inner-timeout test that launches a harmless descendant and proves the complete process tree is gone
a Windows-specific profile/port cleanup assertion after Node termination
recommended_remediation: Make Python own a killable process tree, for example with a Windows job object or an explicit runner/browser PID protocol, and terminate that tree before raising the timeout assertion. Preserve the JavaScript finally path for normal completion and add a forced-timeout regression test.
remediation_risk: Medium: process-tree termination is platform-specific and must target only the disposable test tree, never unrelated browser sessions or operator processes.
validation_rung: Rung 1 focused helper tests plus a synthetic browser-child timeout and Windows process/profile cleanup proof; representative real-media validation is not required.
prior_audit_relationship: The interrupted W11 evidence established bounded normal cleanup but had not closed the ownership gap on Python's timeout branch. This resumed review followed both process owners through the exact helper and generated prelude and confirmed the orphan scenario.

title: Six reviewed WebView test sources are joined to stale PROJECT_INDEX hashes
observed_behavior: docs/generated/PROJECT_INDEX.jsonl records source_hash values that do not match the current bytes of these six test modules. The run-monitor browser summary is also stale, and the metrics summary repeatedly lagged its concurrently changing source during the resumed audit.
expected_invariant: Generated navigation and source summaries used for AI routing must bind each test record to the same current source hash that its semantic review attests, or the stale relationship must remain explicit and finding-backed.
root_cause: The test sources changed after the last full generated-index refresh, while partial summary refreshes and source edits did not atomically refresh PROJECT_INDEX and all affected summaries.
failure_scenario: An agent navigates from PROJECT_INDEX or a stale summary and reviews an obsolete dependency/symbol description, misses newly added assertions or routes, or claims current generated-context evidence for source bytes that the index never represented.
evidence: exact structured joins found PROJECT_INDEX mismatches for all five listed current source paths
test_webview_browser_run_monitor_smoke.py has a generated-summary SHA that also differs from its current source SHA
the metrics source changed repeatedly during this resumed audit while its generated summary and frozen coverage row lagged behind
the other reviewed WebView source-to-index joins matched at the final scoped comparison

Current test_webview_priority_queue_export.py SHA-256 9486ce1db8b4ded403610df4968ad286c4b3eaf47bee5dd92a67d9b0186b3991 is joined to stale PROJECT_INDEX source_hash fd0e6426a83aaeeb80006c0f4f16fb0120987306878b82f53114e32700704b86.
affected_flows: AI repository navigation for WebView tests
incremental summary and project-index refresh workflows
existing_safeguards: coverage rows retain exact source SHA-256 values
generated summaries expose a sha256 front-matter field
repository audit validation requires stale_with_finding rather than silently accepting mismatched PROJECT_INDEX records
safeguard_gap: The refresh workflow permits source, summary, and PROJECT_INDEX updates to land at different times, so consumers can observe a mixed generation without a single atomic freshness gate.
tests_present: repository_audit_ledger validates PROJECT_INDEX reconciliation on reviewed coverage rows
tests_missing: an atomic changed-source check that refreshes or rejects both summary and PROJECT_INDEX drift in one operation
a pre-publication guard proving every reviewed source hash matches all generated navigation records
recommended_remediation: Regenerate PROJECT_INDEX and the two stale summaries from the settled worktree using canonical tooling, then run generator --check modes and repository-audit current-content validation. Consider making the refresh transaction atomic or failing when a partial refresh leaves mixed hashes.
remediation_risk: Low for regeneration; medium for changing refresh orchestration because generated ownership and deterministic ordering must remain intact.
validation_rung: Generated-context regeneration checks, PROJECT_INDEX/source exact-hash join, active-document/reference checks, and the scoped repository-audit fragment validator; representative real-media validation is not required.
prior_audit_relationship: AUDIT-FIND-COV-001 establishes the repository-wide generated-context drift. This W11 finding supplies the exact path-local test-source locations required by strict review-row reconciliation and adds the metrics drift observed during the resumed handoff.
